thread:
oncall-bot: PAGER: Dedicated pool routing error rate > 8% for /v1/generate (dedicated-eu-2). Possible fallback-loop detected. Paging primary oncall. incident_id=INC-2026-1785622341 :rotating_light:

maya_oncall: acked, I'm on it. Pulling dashboards and checking router logs now.

jane_sre: I see a spike in router 'fallback' actions hitting the same model variant with status 503. Seems like smart-routing is repeatedly failing to find a healthy replica and falling back to region EU -> US -> EU in quick succession.

alex_runtime: omg that sounds like the policy we rolled yesterday. The fallback policy had both region and model-variant fallbacks enabled with aggressive backoff disabled. Possible thrash.

maya_oncall: timeline from metrics: 2026-03-15T09:02 -> sudden drop in successful requests, 09:03 router started routing to fallback-variant: 'redwood-llama-8b-quant', 09:04 many of those returned 503, 09:04:15 router re-evaluated and sent to us-east, 09:04:30 back to eu-variant. Oscillation every ~15s.

ops-bot: Recent autoscaler decisions for pool dedicated-eu-2:
```
2026-03-15T09:01:34 - scale_down -> replicas 3
2026-03-15T09:02:50 - scale_up -> replicas 6 (manual override?)
2026-03-15T09:03:40 - scale_down -> replicas 2
```
Looks like conflicting signals — the capacity metric (inflight_tokens) is noisy due to repeated fallback requests.

tiago_eng: That explains the blackholing — when the router sees low capacity it pushes to fallback targets; those fail and the router misinterprets that as capacity still low and keeps moving traffic, plus scaler sees low utilization and keeps shrinking. vicious loop.

maya_oncall: Immediate mitigation plan: 1) disable smart-routing fallbacks for affected paths, 2) pin /v1/generate to dedicated-eu-2 model variant 'redwood-llama-8b-quant' temporarily, 3) force scale dedicated-eu-2 to 8 replicas. Executing 1 & 3 now.

maya_oncall: Running command: `redwoodctl routing update --path /v1/generate --smart-fallback false --policy temporary-no-fallback`

deploy-bot: routing config change accepted by control-plane (cfg-id: cfg_1785622341_route_1). Propagating to routers (progress: 2/4 routers applied).

maya_oncall: Scaling pool: `redwoodctl pools resize --pool dedicated-eu-2 --replicas 8 --reason "incident INC-2026-1785622341"`

ops-bot: Scale request acked, new replicas provisioning. ETA ~70s.

jane_sre: While that lands, I'm going to temporarily mute the fallback policy in the router: editing policy file snippet below and setting backoff to true + max_retries=1 is safer long-term, but for now full disable as Maya did is good.

jane_sre: policy snippet we changed:
```
- name: region_and_variant_fallback
  enabled: true -> false
  max_retries: 3 -> 1
  backoff: false -> true
```

alex_runtime: I also pushed a quick fix to treat 503 from fallback target as 'do not count toward capacity signal' for 30s, preventing scaler thrash. will monitor. change-id: rtm-3642.

tiago_eng: Noted. Can someone confirm that CS-facing latency is back to acceptable range?

maya_oncall: Grafana now shows success rate recovering: errors down from 8.4% -> 1.2% in the last 3m. p95 latency for /v1/generate trending down from 1.8s -> 350ms.

cs_liaison: Heads up: we started getting customer pings about timeouts from a small subset in EU. I've informed Support to message impacted customers with a short update: "We've detected a routing incident impacting EU requests; mitigation in progress, no model data was altered."

qa_lead: I see a couple of failed eval runs that triggered around 09:01 which might have contributed to the sudden load on fallback variants. Those runs used the experimental quantized variant. Logging them for follow-up.

ops-bot: Routers applied new routing config: 4/4. Pool replicas: provisioning -> healthy(8) in 64s.

deploy-bot: control-plane note: automated policy rollback scheduled? none. Change tagged as incident-temporary.

maya_oncall: Ok i'm going to keep fallback disabled and monitor for 30 minutes. I'm handing off to @jane_sre for the next shift to own the follow-up (longer-term policy tuning + postmortem).

jane_sre: taking handoff. I'll coordinate with Tiago and Alex to land the config hygiene and add a safety gate in the autoscaler to ignore fallback-induced capacity dips.

alex_runtime: I'll open a PR to change default fallback backoff and a test that simulates a fallback loop. assign to triage. rtm-pr-3643.

tiago_eng: Also recommend we add a router metric 'fallback_loop_count' and an alert when >5 in 1m so we can page earlier.

maya_oncall: Thank you all. Incident level: Sev-2. Customer-impact: partial for EU region, mostly timeouts and higher latency for some tenants. No data loss.

cs_liaison: Logged impacted customers and sent messages. Keeping watch for any escalations.

jane_sre: I'll create an incident ticket and postmortem stub: INC-2026-1785622341-pm. Tags: routing, autoscale, fallback-policy, dedicated-pool. Due: 2026-03-18.

maya_oncall: Handoff complete. Ending live mitigation. If anyone sees oscillation reappear ping me directly. :white_check_mark:

oncall-bot: NOTE: Next oncall handoff scheduled. Incident flagged for postmortem, owners: jane_sre, alex_runtime, tiago_eng.

jane_sre: quick retrospective note in-thread: root cause summary -> combination of aggressive fallback policy + failure mode where fallback targets return 503 causing router to misinterpret as capacity signal, which fed autoscaler contradictory metrics. Remediation items:
- enforce backoff / lower retries on fallback policies
- autoscaler: ignore transient 503 spikes when fallback flag is set
- router: short-circuit multi-region oscillation by tagging request history and preventing immediate cross-region bounce
- alerting: add fallback-loop alarm (as Tiago suggested)

alex_runtime: I will also coordinate a canary test for routing changes before they hit dedicated pools.

cs_liaison: I'll prepare a short customer note summarizing impact and fixes after the postmortem is published.

maya_oncall: last check: error rate steady at 0.8% for 10m, p95 stable under 400ms. marking incident as mitigated.

oncall-bot: INCIDENT UPDATE: mitigated at 2026-03-15T09:56:39. Closing active pager.
